research_context.original_topic: How are pulsars formed? Pulsars are rotating neutron stars that produce pulses of radio waves, X-rays, and gamma rays. They form when a massive star runs out of fuel and collapses in on itself. The remnant is a neutron star with a strong magnetic field. The research should distinguish isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down from binary recycling and companion-ablation evolution, and test formation and evolution with mathematical models.
